Wave 2 is the correction of that impulse, not the start of a wave 3. By the rules alone no trigger comes either: B (1.5505) is never closed above within EM3, and the end of wave 2 breaks on 08-30.
notes: Shortlist #19 of candidates.md ("FAIL 2026-08-30; spike wave 1, 15M available"). Chain H4 / H1 / 15M. Log lengths 0.142 / 0.212 / 0.323: an extended fifth. The scan flags the candidate as "chained: W5 or later" (strategy.md, Counting Across 1-2s): its wave 1 is wave 5, and 1.6999 -> 1.3574 corrects the whole impulse (41.3 % of 0.9862 -> 1.6999). Wave 1 of the candidate: 1.2303 -> 1.6999 = log 0.323; the last two H4 candles (from 1.4229) hold 55 % of it. The top is a liquidation spike: 08-22 05:00 (15M) runs from 1.6628 to 1.6999 and down to 1.3780 at 7.1x volume and closes 1.5286. Wave 2: 69.6 % by the wick (78.6 % = 1.3184), no close beyond it (EM1). On 15M and H1: A 1.3780 (in the spike candle), B 1.5505 (08-25 02:30, 56 % of A), C 1.3574 (08-26 15:00), C/A 0.63: a zigzag (EM2). Because A sits in the same 15M candle as the end of wave 1, the scan cannot see it on H4 (tools/README.md, Limit). EM3: wave 2 lasted 4.4 days (08-22 05:00 to 08-26 15:00); the window ends about 08-31 01:00. EM4: after C the highest 15M close is 1.4732 (08-27 16:30), far below B: no trigger. The end of wave 2 breaks on 08-30 20:00 (low 1.3352). Afterwards: 1.3098 (09-02) and 1.2468 (09-16, 57 % of 0.9862 -> 1.6999), a rally to 1.6581 (09-23) below the spike high, and back to 1.2546 (10-24): a range of 1.25 to 1.70, no wave 3 so far. What the case shows: a spike wave 1 puts B high (here at 1.5505, 71.5 % back up wave 1), so the trigger needs most of the spike back, as in xrpusdt-d1-2025-03-long. The counting step (W5 or later) would have flagged it already. Open question (for the strategy): - A wave 1 whose end is a single liquidation wick (one 15M candle with the high of wave 1 and the low of A): should the end of wave 1 be measured from the highest close (1.6628) instead of the wick? EM1 would then read 67.4 %.
